newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac raps Jospin over French Central Africa role.
newsitem.headline: Chirac raps Jospin over French Central Africa role.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac hit out at Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin on Wednesday for criticising French military retaliation for the killing of two soldiers by army mutineers in the Central African Republic.

"The president made known his surprise that some political leaders should propose that France not react when its soldiers are publicly murdered in cold blood," government spokesman Alain Lamassoure told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
"No one should count on France not to react when its soldiers are killed," he quoted Chirac as saying.

Jospin warned the government on Monday against being sucked into military escalation in the Central African Republic and acting as a bodyguard for disputed President Ange-Felix Patasse after the weekend violence.

The French military, in what Paris called legitimate self-defence, launched an artillery and helicopter attack on the mutineers on Sunday, killing about 10 people, after the unarmed French soldiers, accompanying African mediators, were shot in the back on Saturday.

Foreign Minister Herve de Charette told the cabinet that France still did not intend to get involved in a political settlement to the crisis, but was backing the efforts of the African mediators headed by Malian General Amadou Toumani Toure.
